newsitem.title: BELARUS: Europe rights body condemns Belarus referendum.
newsitem.headline: Europe rights body condemns Belarus referendum.

text.p: A team from Europe's top human rights body said on Wednesday a referendum in Belarus that gave President Alexander Lukashenko sweeping powers was illegitimate.

"A number of facts concerning the run-up to the referendum makes it impossible for our delegation to reach a positive conclusion as to the democratic legitimacy of the referendum and its results," said the leader of a Council of Europe group.

Chairman Tadeusz Iwinski of Poland said a lack of media access for some political forces in the ex-Soviet republic meant genuine political debate on Lukashenko's draft constitution and a rival proposed by parliament had not taken place.

Lukashenko monopolised state television, radio and leading newspapers and won the votes of more than 70 percent of the electorate on Sunday for his plans to extend his term by two years and reorganise other institutions.

A Council of Europe statement called on Lukashenko to "respect parliamentary democracy and the rule of law," and expressed concern that the way a new legislature was being formed could deprive parliament of its legitimacy.
About 110 deputies have accepted Lukashenko's invitation to form a new parliament, leaving some 60 deputies who oppose him sitting in the official parliament hall.
The statement said the way the referendum was organised "was contrary to democratic standards and jeopardised the future of democratic development in Belarus".
The delegates held a two-hour meeting with Lukashenko which their chairman described as "two monologues rather than a dialogue".
Lukashenko had asked what Belarus -- the only European country outside former Yugoslavia which has not joined the Council -- would have to do to become a member, Iwinski said.
They told him Belarus could join as soon as it had met minimum standards on democracy and human rights.
